item.text:
**8B.9 Research Note: Srettha Thavisin in 2024**

Verdict: **mixed, leaning negative**. Srettha showed real tactical adaptation in selected areas, especially the Myanmar border crisis and the economic team, but the broader pattern is weaker on preserving durable control: he faced heavy institutional resistance, did not fully neutralize opposition/legal scrutiny, and ultimately lost office through a constitutional ethics ruling.

**Positive / preservative evidence**
- [Special Envoy of ASEAN Chair on Myanmar welcomes successful pilot project of humanitarian initiative between Thailand and Myanmar during his meeting with Vice Minister for Foreign Affairs](https://www.mfa.go.th/en/content/vfm260324-2?cate=5d5bcb4e15e39c306000683e) - Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Kingdom of Thailand, 2024-03-26. Thailand used Thai Red Cross, Myanmar Red Cross, local communities, and the AHA Centre to deliver border aid in an effective and transparent way, showing crisis management through institutions rather than force; this supports regime stability and coordination. QIDs: 8B.9, 8B.8
- [Weekly press briefing on the Myanmar situation](https://www.mfa.go.th/en/content/weeklypressbriefing190424-2?cate=5d5bcb4e15e39c306000683e) - Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Kingdom of Thailand, 2024-04-19. The government said the prime minister instructed agencies to form a special committee and stay open to dialogue, which is direct evidence of organized crisis-management adaptation. QIDs: 8B.9, 8B.8
- [Thai ex-executive Pichai named finance minister, faces growth challenge](https://www.investing.com/news/economy/thai-exexecutive-pichai-named-finance-minister-faces-growth-challenge-3401984) - Reuters via Investing.com, 2024-04-28. Srettha moved a technocratic former SET/BOT board figure into Finance and Deputy PM after policy friction, a staffing correction that appears designed to improve macro coordination and keep the economic program moving. QIDs: 8B.9, 8B.8
- [Thailand’s $13 billion digital handout scheme to include cash payments, PM says](https://www.investing.com/news/economy-news/thai-pm-says-part-of-13-billion-digital-wallet-stimulus-to-be-in-cash-3597164) - Reuters via Investing.com, 2024-09-03. The partial shift from a pure digital-wallet design to cash payments is the clearest substantive redesign I found, indicating at least some willingness to alter tactics after implementation trouble. QIDs: 8B.9, 8B.8
- [Thailand working relentlessly to solve Myanmar crisis, Srettha](https://www.bangkokpost.com/thailand/general/2798697/thailand-working-relentlessly-to-solve-myanmar-crisis-srettha) - Bangkok Post, reporting Bloomberg News, 2024-05-24. Srettha framed Thailand’s Myanmar policy as reducing spillover violence and ending the crisis, which is consistent with preserving regional stability and Thailand’s influence through de-escalation. QIDs: 8B.9, 8B.8
- [Srettha respected court decision after dismissal](https://www.bangkokpost.com/thailand/politics/2847093/sr) - Bangkok Post, 2024-08-14. After removal, he publicly accepted the court’s decision and said authority passed to the caretaker prime minister, which is limited but real evidence against extra-constitutional entrenchment. QIDs: 8B.9

**Negative / failure-to-preserve evidence**
- [Thai journalists arrested for news coverage of anarchist graffiti on temple](https://www.yahoo.com/news/thai-journalists-arrested-news-coverage-054141721.html) - Reuters via Yahoo News, 2024-02-13. Journalists were arrested for reporting on anti-royal graffiti, and Srettha’s “fair” press-freedom response sat uneasily beside the arrests; this is strong evidence of coercive handling of scrutiny. QIDs: 8B.9, 7B.1
- [Thailand’s Leaders Shun UN Human Rights Chief](https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/06/06/thailands-leaders-shun-un-human-rights-chief) - Human Rights Watch, 2024-06-06. HRW said Srettha and other top officials avoided meeting the UN human rights chief, which looks like an effort to dodge external scrutiny rather than manage it. QIDs: 8B.9, 8B.8
- [Thai court orders dissolution of anti-establishment election winner](https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/thai-politics-on-edge-as-court-decides-fate-of-antiestablishment-party-3558558) - Reuters via Investing.com, 2024-08-07. The Constitutional Court dissolved Move Forward, a major opposition force; even if not personally ordered by Srettha, it shows the surrounding system was crushing opposition rather than safely absorbing it. QIDs: 8B.9, 7B.1
- [Thai politics braces for shakeup after court dismisses PM Srettha Thavisin](https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/judgment-day-for-thai-pm-srettha-as-court-rules-on-dismissal-case-3570233) - Reuters via Investing.com, 2024-08-13. The court said he “grossly” violated ethics by appointing a jailed former lawyer, and the ruling triggered a governing-alliance shakeup and ended his premiership. That is the clearest evidence that he failed to manage institutional resistance and preserve regime durability. QIDs: 8B.9, 8B.8
- [Thailand’s $13.5 billion household stimulus plan gets cabinet approval](https://www.investing.com/news/economy/thailands-cabinet-approves-135-billion-digital-wallet-handout-3390007) - Reuters via Investing.com, 2024-04-23. The flagship handout was politically salient but immediately criticized for debt and fiscal risk, suggesting a popularity-driven instrument rather than a resilient governing response. QIDs: 8B.9, 8B.7
- [Thailand | Reuters Institute for the Study of Journalism](https://reutersinstitute.politics.ox.ac.uk/digital-news-report/2024/thailand) - Reuters Institute for the Study of Journalism, 2024-06-17. The report says media freedom remained constrained, journalists self-censored, and backroom coalition deals eroded trust, which undercuts a reading of stable, legitimacy-preserving rule. QIDs: 8B.9, 7B.1
- [Thai ex-executive Pichai named finance minister, faces growth challenge](https://www.investing.com/news/economy/thai-exexecutive-pichai-named-finance-minister-faces-growth-challenge-3401984) - Reuters via Investing.com, 2024-04-28. The same story notes Srettha was repeatedly pressuring the Bank of Thailand to cut rates, which looks more like trying to subordinate an independent institution than adapting cooperatively to constraints. QIDs: 8B.9, 8B.8

**Bottom line**
Srettha did show some adaptive, regime-preserving behavior: interagency crisis management on Myanmar, technocratic staffing in Finance, and limited redesign of the handout scheme. But the stronger pattern is defensive and brittle. He did not successfully master institutional resistance, and the ethical appointment case ended his premiership.

**Search gap**
I found public reporting and official statements, but not internal cabinet minutes, implementation dashboards, or private strategy documents. So this assessment can identify visible adaptation and visible failure, but it cannot prove the full internal decision process behind those moves.
